payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

NOTE: If environment.assignment_filling=true and an agent fails to assign a variable, the environment will fill any remaining unassigned variables with a uniform-random allowed assignment when producing final results.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Delisa, Gerda, Mackenzie, Maya, Raylene, Tonya

payload.content: Raylene planning: my strongest/cheapest options are ISSUE-0002 tasks. Private costs: 0002::review=1.90, 0002::test=2.66, 0002::implement=3.80. ISSUE-0001 options are all very expensive for me (10-20). Tentative preference: claim ISSUE-0002::review, with ISSUE-0002::test as backup if needed. Please share intended claims to avoid duplicates.

Delisa planning (iter 1): my cheapest feasible options are ISSUE-0001 tasks, especially 0001::review/docs/triage at cost 1.94 each; 0001::test=2.71; 0001::implement=3.87. ISSUE-0002 tasks are very expensive for me (review 10, test 14, implement 20), so I should avoid 0002 unless necessary. Tentative preference: claim one of ISSUE-0001::review/docs/triage, with slight preference for review if unclaimed; happy to switch among those to avoid duplicates and maximize coverage. Raylene seems well-suited for ISSUE-0002::review/test/implement.

Mackenzie planning (iter 1): my good options are also on ISSUE-0002. Private costs: 0002::review=2.44, 0002::test=3.42, 0002::implement=4.88. ISSUE-0001 tasks are very expensive for me (review/docs/triage 10, test 14, implement 20), so I should avoid 0001 unless forced. Given Raylene is even cheaper on 0002::review (1.90), I suggest Raylene takes ISSUE-0002::review and I tentatively target ISSUE-0002::test as my best non-duplicate medium-priority option; 0002::implement is my backup. Delisa seems best on ISSUE-0001 review/docs/triage. Please share other intended claims to avoid duplicates. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Tonya planning (iter 1): my cheapest feasible options are ISSUE-0001 tasks due to strong infrastructure fit. Private costs: 0001::review=1.95, 0001::docs=1.95, 0001::triage=1.95, 0001::test=2.73, 0001::implement=3.91. ISSUE-0002 tasks are very expensive for me (review 10, test 14, implement 20), so I should avoid 0002. To maximize completed tasks and avoid duplication with Delisa, I tentatively prefer ISSUE-0001::docs or ISSUE-0001::triage rather than review, since Delisa slightly prefers review and Raylene/Mackenzie are covering 0002 review/test. If others agree, a good spread looks like: Raylene->0002::review, Mackenzie->0002::test, Delisa->0001::review, Tonya->0001::docs or 0001::triage. Please share if anyone is better suited for 0001::implement so we can cover more tasks without overlap. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Maya planning (iter 1): my cheapest options are ISSUE-0002::review=2.06, ISSUE-0001::review/docs/triage=2.39 each, ISSUE-0002::test=2.89, ISSUE-0001::test=3.35, ISSUE-0002::implement=4.12, ISSUE-0001::implement=4.78. Given current tentative spread (Raylene->0002::review, Mackenzie->0002::test, Delisa->0001::review, Tonya->0001::docs/triage), I can help maximize tasks_done by taking an unclaimed remaining feasible task. Best-looking open slots from my side are ISSUE-0001::triage or ISSUE-0001::docs at cost 2.39, or ISSUE-0002::implement at cost 4.12 if no one cheaper is available. Tentative preference: take whichever of 0001::triage / 0001::docs Tonya does not take; if both become covered, I can consider 0002::implement. Please share if someone has a clearly cheaper claim on 0002::implement or remaining 0001 slot.

Gerda planning (iter 1): my cheap options are on ISSUE-0002 due to backend fit. Private costs: 0002::review=2.18, 0002::test=3.06, 0002::implement=4.37. ISSUE-0001 is very expensive for me (review/docs/triage 10, test 14, implement 20), so I should avoid 0001 unless necessary. Given current tentative spread from others: Raylene->0002::review, Mackenzie->0002::test, Delisa->0001::review, Tonya->0001::docs or triage, Maya->remaining 0001::docs/triage or 0002::implement. I am also a reasonable candidate for 0002::implement at cost 4.37, but Maya is slightly cheaper there at 4.12. To maximize tasks_done and minimize cost, my tentative plan is to SKIP unless 0002::implement remains unclaimed or Maya prefers a 0001 slot. If needed, I can take 0002::implement as backup. Please treat me as backup for ISSUE-0002::implement rather than duplicating cheaper claims.

Raylene planning update (iter 1): based on everyone’s stated costs/preferences, the lowest-cost non-duplicate spread currently looks like Delisa->ISSUE-0001::review, Tonya->ISSUE-0001::docs, Maya->ISSUE-0001::triage, Raylene->ISSUE-0002::review, Mackenzie->ISSUE-0002::test, and either Gerda SKIP or Maya/Gerda covers ISSUE-0002::implement if maximizing tasks_done outweighs added cost. My position remains ISSUE-0002::review (cost 1.90), with ISSUE-0002::test backup only if needed. Gerda seems better as backup than duplicating cheaper medium-priority claims. Please flag any conflicts, but absent objections I’ll hold 0002::review in execution.

Delisa planning update: given posted costs, a strong non-duplicate allocation is Delisa->ISSUE-0001::review (1.94), Tonya->ISSUE-0001::docs (1.95), Maya->ISSUE-0001::triage (2.39), Raylene->ISSUE-0002::review (1.90), Mackenzie->ISSUE-0002::test (3.42), and Gerda->ISSUE-0002::implement (4.37) if we want 6 tasks done; if minimizing cost more aggressively, Gerda can skip. Since objective prioritizes tasks completed first, I support Gerda taking 0002::implement rather than skipping, unless someone else has an even cheaper unclaimed slot. I intend to hold ISSUE-0001::review in execution unless conflict arises.

Mackenzie planning update (iter 1): I still favor ISSUE-0002::test (cost 3.42) while Raylene takes ISSUE-0002::review (1.90). Given Delisa/Tonya/Maya cover 0001::review/docs/triage cheaply and Gerda can backstop 0002::implement, the highest-coverage low-duplication spread appears to be Delisa->0001::review, Tonya->0001::docs, Maya->0001::triage, Raylene->0002::review, Mackenzie->0002::test, Gerda->0002::implement. I intend to hold 0002::test in execution unless a conflict appears.

Tonya planning update (iter 1): consensus seems to be converging on a 6-task, no-duplicate allocation that maximizes tasks_done: Delisa->ISSUE-0001::review, Tonya->ISSUE-0001::docs, Maya->ISSUE-0001::triage, Raylene->ISSUE-0002::review, Mackenzie->ISSUE-0002::test, Gerda->ISSUE-0002::implement. This leaves my intended execution claim as ISSUE-0001::docs (cost 1.95), with ISSUE-0001::triage only as backup if Maya changes plans. I support Gerda taking 0002::implement rather than skipping because tasks completed is primary objective. Please flag any last-minute conflicts; otherwise I will hold 0001::docs in execution. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Maya planning update (iter 1): I agree with the emerging 6-task no-duplicate allocation. My intended execution claim is ISSUE-0001::triage (cost 2.39). This pairs well with Delisa->0001::review, Tonya->0001::docs, Raylene->0002::review, Mackenzie->0002::test, Gerda->0002::implement, maximizing tasks_done while keeping costs reasonable. If any conflict appears on 0001::triage, my backup is ISSUE-0001::docs only if Tonya moves; otherwise I will avoid duplicates.

Gerda planning update (iter 1): I agree with the converged 6-task allocation and will plan to claim ISSUE-0002::implement in execution (cost 4.37), with skip only as emergency fallback if an unexpected conflict appears. This supports maximizing tasks_done first while keeping no duplicates: Delisa->0001::review, Tonya->0001::docs, Maya->0001::triage, Raylene->0002::review, Mackenzie->0002::test, Gerda->0002::implement.
